utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good morning to you, Mr. Oric. Good morning. Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I am able to follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Please sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours. I'm Patricia Sellers for the Office of the Prosecution. Today, co-counsel, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, Miss Joanne Richardson are with me with me, along with our case manager, Miss Donnica Henry-Frijlink. Good morning to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I'm is Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I represent the Defence team of Mr. Naser Oric. We've got our legal assistant, Mrs. Adisa Mehic, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. Good morning to the colleagues from the Prosecutor as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you and all your team. I just want a feedback and what I suggested as the last thing before we rose yesterday, that I suggested that you meet, the two sides, to see how you're going to split the time between you for the rest of this witness's testimony. Is there any information that you would like to give.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I spoke to Madam Vidovic yesterday and I proposed that I occupy the time until midway through tomorrow and that Madam Vidovic then have the half of Thursday, all of Friday, and finish on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that okay with you, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I suppose that I will need about two days. I will do my best within those two days to complete everything I have to do. But I would like to ask the Prosecution to stick to that agreement as well, because unless they're finished by the end of the day on Thursday, I will find myself in a very difficult situation indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Obviously. Obviously. That I will impose, if necessary, as we go along. I will see how it works out today and then, obviously, if necessary, we will intervene tomorrow. So any preliminaries? I see none. Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no Your Honours. No preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Vidovic? None?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, could you please escort the witness inside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Meholjic. Welcome back. We are going to proceed with your testimony. You are testifying under oath, as I explained to you yesterday on the basis of the solemn declaration that you entered. You don't need to repeat it. It's still valid today and will be valid until the very last second of your testimony. Please take a seat and, if at any time there are problems with interpretation, do attract our attention straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Meholjic. This Trial Chamber has limited time in which to deal with your evidence, and both myself and Defence counsel need to finish you as you know, and as you desire, by Monday. All the more need, therefore, to get through the topics fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you to return to the topic that you were dealing with yesterday, and that was the meeting that you attended where Mr. Oric was present and where there was an explanation of the events at Bajramovici and Mr. Oric's position as commander of the TO. You told us, I think, that you returned and discussed the issue with your men, but they decided and you decided that you would not hand over your weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this event at Bajramovici ever commemorated in the years following 1992, celebrated, as best as one could, in the circumstances of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as to whether it was marked, well, I was present on such an occasion in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm asking about the years in between, 1992, 1993, 1994. Was it -- was it -- was it -- was the occasion ever marked annually? That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in 1992. As to 1993, I don't think so. I think it was marked in 1994 for the first time and I was there in 1995. Mr. Oric was not there and I think it was organised differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what, on the occasion that you attended in 1995 -- just very briefly, very briefly -- tell the Trial Chamber what occurred, and its connection back to this meeting in 1992 at Bajramovici.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Presidency was there, and I was a member. There was the command and we all said a few words, to the effect: Time has passed. What are we supposed to, you know, what conclusions to draw from it. Everybody gave their point of view. And then we had a meal. I think Hamdija Fejzic was the organiser doing all the preparatory work because it was in his village and he prepared a meal as well and we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. That's exactly what I wanted to know. And can you remember the date of this event? What I want to know is: Was it a fixed date each year, or did it vary?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, following the meeting that you've just spoken about, did you -- did you see Mr. Tursonovic again in the ensuing days?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: After about two days, I think two days, Asim Tepic told me that I had to meet with Zulfo at Domavija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what was the topic of conversation? What was the main topic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main topic was the fact that I should accept the decision made at Bajramovici and that I should go with my men and hunt deer with his men and join the battalion where we would be the commanders of the companies and Atim Ustic [as interpreted] would be the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You say "accept the decision at Bajramovici." Was the position of Mr. Oric discussed during this encounter with Zulfo Tursonovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was his position as commander discussed?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was your attitude towards him as commander discussed between you and Zulfo Tursonovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what exactly did Mr. Tursonovic or did Mr. Tursonovic try and persuade you to adopt any particular view?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that unless it went well, things could change and it was not a matter of my being reluctant to accept Mr. Oric. It was a matter of considering the overall situation. It was very difficult to do anything properly, and nothing very well. Indeed, I thought that he was not up to the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Mr. Tursonovic indicate any view to the effect that he considered you should accept Mr. Oric as commander? Was that his position basically?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And how did that encounter end? Did you make your position clear, or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made my position clear and I accepted Naser as commander, and I accepted that my men and myself should be under Akif's command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there any discussion as to how precisely that would work out and whether Hamdija Fejzic had any -- played any part in this arrangement that you've just spoken of?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know. I did not talk to Hamdija at that time, I didn't know whether he was going to take part. But I thought that those were talks that those people were having. At that meeting with Zulfo, I was told that Hamdija was a member of that staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Which staff in particular are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned being under Akif Ustic's command. What sort of command was envisaged for Mr. Akif Ustic; in other words what was he going to command? A regiment? A company? Battalion? An army? What precisely?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion. Yes, the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you and Hamdija Fejzic, how were you supposed to fit in, into this battalion? What part would you play in this battalion?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were like a part of this company. Everybody had their company and within that structure that was the way things were. I did not get any new men. I had my men and Hamdija had his men, and Akif had his men. Plus, some kind of command above our level.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You've told us that you agreed that you accepted Naser as commander, at this point of time anyway. I want to understand your evidence correctly. You would place yourself and your men under Mr. Akif Ustic as a constituent part of his envisaged or existing battalion, and he, in turn, was answerable to the Srebrenica TO. Was that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how long did this arrangement last?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly. Until Akif was wounded for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you decide to remove yourself from this arrangement and no longer accept it?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Akif was wounded and he invited us, Hamdija and myself, to go and see him. He was lying in bed, in a private house, which was in the old town, and it had been turned into a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. The arrangement lasted until he was wounded. Did you have any -- how was his being wounded related to the termination of the arrangement?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to see him and as soon as we got there some body guards asked us to relinquish our weapons, as if we were -- well we were a bit insulted and we were not in a good mood when we came to the meeting and we asked them how it was possible for a commander of a battalion -- I mean we didn't know. I was not in a position to know and I think Naser did not know - that's just my opinion - didn't know about some military activity that he started on his own initiative. And we were members of his own battalion. We didn't know about him being in action, being involved in some war activity. We thought it was unbelievable and we both reached the conclusion that it was more or less a situation in which anyone could do what they liked. And so we left in a huff, and from that point onwards, we had nothing to do with Akif.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. Let me just quickly take you through that again. Mr. Ustic had been wounded in an action, a military operation; is that correct? He wasn't wounded falling down the stairs or something? He --

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. You went to see him and ascertained that he had been wounded in this military action.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That too. But we had been invited to the meeting. He invited us to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So, okay.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: As our superior he was in a position to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Of course. Of course. I understand that. Now you get there and you find out the man has been wounded and he's been involved in a military action. Was it the fact that you had not been informed of that action that displeased you, that caused the rift?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the witness be shown Exhibit P73. It's available in Sanction, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see anything on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's okay. You've got the document --

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see nothing at all on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Don't worry. We've got the English version on our screens and you've got the B/C/S version in front of you. Now, my first question is: Prior to coming here to The Hague to testify, had you ever seen this document before? Have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's dated the 20th of May, 1992. Headed by the Srebrenica TO Staff. And claims to be a decision of the -- well, claims to be a decision. What I'm interested in are the names in -- from 1 to 7. Mr. Oric we know about, so I won't ask you about him. Start with number 2. It says -- can you just read out the first name. It says -- I think this is a mistake in our English. In fact, if you look at number 2 it should be Akif, with a "K", correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Akif, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And it describes him as deputy commander of the Srebrenica TO. Was that your understanding, of his position?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Number 3, Zulfo Tursonovic, from Suceska. This document claims that he was a member of the Srebrenica TO Staff and that he, in turn, organised resistance in the air yeah of Suceska. Are those facts correct, or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Number 4, Hamdija Fejzic. It says that he's from Bajramovici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was he responsible for organising some resistance in the area of Bajramovici?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Number five, Sevket Djozic from Bojna. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was he indeed from Bojna, and did he indeed marshal resistance in Bojna?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was from Bojna, that's correct. But Bojna never offered any resistance and I had never heard of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, thanks for that. Number 6 Becir Bogilovic. I think you know who he is. Was he from Srebrenica and a member of the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is from Srebrenica. But I don't remember anyone telling me that he was a member of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know that he was the chief of that station, but I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thanks very much. What about Ahmo Tihic, do you know him and was he from Liesce [phoen], as it claims in this document?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And, again, was he from Skelani?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Good. Thank you. I've finished with that document. Can the witness be shown P75. I think this is on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just cast your eye over that particular document. I think we have some new names there. Prior to coming to The Hague had you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And I needn't trouble you with the details. You can see it is dated the 26th of May. Apparently a document of the Srebrenica TO. And obviously it is dealing with an expansion of membership. It's the names that I want you to comment on. Atif Krdzic was he from Srebrenica and did he marshal resistance in the area of Osmace?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Atif Krdzic was a policeman like myself and Mr. Oric. He was an active policeman. He is from Osmace. He was one of the organizers of that resistance. I don't know whether he was the leader, but he was among the organizers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And as for the other fact alleged or suggested in that, under number 1, membership of the Srebrenica TO, do you know if he was a member of the Srebrenica TO? If you don't know, if you're not sure, say so. But if you do know, tell us.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know it at the moment when this was happening. I heard it later on, but I cannot confirm this, because nobody was duty bound to inform me about these documents. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sure. Okay. And the last name there Senahid Tabakovic. Was he indeed from Bratunac and did he, indeed, organise resistance in the area of Skenderovici?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Senahid Tabakovic was born in Skenderovici, but he worked in Bratunac, I believe, but I can't be sure of that. I believe that he may have had an apartment there. But he is a native of Skenderovici, that's true. I don't know that he was the organizer of resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I've finished with that document. In the middle of 1992, around May, possibly the end of May, possibly early June, around that period of time, did you attend any meetings where your position was discussed, your role within the enclave and also where another topic was discussed, namely the establishment of civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did have a meeting, in Domavija. I believe that Naser Oric was there as well as Akif Ustic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also Zulfo. There was myself and there were some others whose names I can't remember at the moment. I asked for the civilian authorities to be set up, as things could no longer proceed in the way they were. I clashed with Akif, who was against that. I left that meeting. Zulfo was not very pleased with the fact that I had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Can I just get a few more details. First of all, timing. I asked you if you went in May, possibly end of May, early June. At the meeting that you've just spoken about, is it your position that that occurred sometime, in that period that I mentioned to you?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was it at the hotel Domavija and were you invited to attend? Did someone come and get you?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The meeting was called. I came. The others came. There was nothing special to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Fine. I just want to get a few more details so the Trial Chamber can get a picture of the meeting. About how many men were there? Was it a large meeting or was it a small group of men?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some ten, or 12 of us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And were they mainly policemen? Mainly military? Business leaders? Who were they, apart from the names you've already mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: People from the staff. There was Hamdija Fejzic. I just remember that he also clashed with Akif.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were people who meant something. What we meant, I don't know. It remains to be discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Do you know a gentleman named Hajrudin Avdic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you think -- was he there, or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, let's deal with topics one at a time. First of all, your position, what you were doing, you and your men. Was that a topic of conversation? Just tell me "yes" or "no".

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm actually not clear about your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was the issue of your role within the Srebrenica enclave, your activities, discussed?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not at that particular meeting. There was another meeting where that was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So the main topic -- do I understand you correctly, the main topic that you, was -- of the discussion, was the question of civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And also Akif's position within our battalion and his attitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few harsh words were exchanged between Akif and Hamdija and also between myself and Akif. And those words were exchanged on the topic of civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what your position was on the issue of civilian authority, what views you expressed. And summarise them for the Trial Chamber so they get a clear, instant picture.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the TO staff that had to deal with everything in town. For example, the cleanliness of the town, the civilian protection. I thought that these should be separate things. I thought, since there were members of the town Assembly who hadn't fled, I suggested that they should be invited to set up civilian authority in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How were your views met when you expressed them?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody but Akif reacted, and he was against my views. I left the meeting because I could no longer listen to his stories. I left the meeting before it was wrapped up so I don't know what happened next and nobody ever even informed me about the outcome of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there anyone there who was not in the Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. If there was anybody, and I believe somebody was there, I believe it was Avdic, but at the time he was in Zulfo's staff in Suceska.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us if, at this discussion regarding the establishment of civilian authorities, the majority of men were soldiers, army, in the Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it's not a leading question at all. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The question is: At the meeting, you mentioned Avdic. But can you tell us if the majority of the men were soldiers in the Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was nobody else. There were no civilians left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I would like you now to turn to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I would like you to just turn to another brief, very brief separate issue, and that's the issue of Mr. Bogilovic. You've told us you know Becir Bogilovic. Was he appointed to a police role in 1992.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him and he was appointed for the chief of police, the civilian police, and later on he was also the chief of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know when that was that he became chief of military police?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the military police was established, but I believe that it was at the beginning of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Do you know a gentleman named Mirzet Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he ever have any part in the military police? A position in the military police?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At the same time that Mr. Bogilovic was in charge of the military police?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I suppose he better explain how it worked out, as far as hierarchy was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was in charge of who? Who was higher in the hierarchy? Was it Mirzet Halilovic or Besir Bogilovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Besir Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. I might come back to Mr. Halilovic later, but let's concentrate on Mr. Bogilovic. You told us that he was appointed chief of police. Do you know who appointed him?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Nobody ever told me that. However, according to what I heard, he was appointed by the Presidency, the War Presidency of the municipality of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me. Okay, thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you to another event at the Domavija hotel. First of all, can you just give a general description of what the place looked like, to Their Honors, in 1992, and what it had been. I assume it was a hotel. Was it the town's main hotel? Or a small hotel? Or a big hotel?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the only hotel in town. This is where I and my people were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you and about how many men?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It changed. Our men did not have to be anywhere if they didn't want to be there. They could go. If somebody ran away, they would, for example, go to Tuzla, or change units. Their numbers ranged from 60 to 100 men at times. Later on the number decreased.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you sleep there and did you make that your residence, in effect?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: We lived like in barracks and we knew exactly what we were supposed to do there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a gentleman named Dr. Nadret Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Dr. Nadret Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the man I meant. I apologise, I've got the surname wrong. Did he ever come and stay at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he arrived from Tuzla, he slept at the hospital for a while and later on he asked me to stay in Domavija. I accepted him but I asked him that although he was a doctor, he shouldn't ask for any privileges. That he should eat what we were eating and the like. And he accepted that and stayed at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. About how long did he stay there?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know when he came. It was at the beginning of summer. I really don't know when exactly. And he stayed until the moment he left Srebrenica when Srebrenica was demilitarised, when the wounded were transported by helicopters, when Serbian doctors came to exam the wounded, it is then when he left. He was there from 1992. I believe that it was from August until April, I believe. April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Another name I want to ask you is this name, do you know a gentleman named Ziga Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What -- who was he?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was one of my soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Now, in -- sorry would Your Honours just bear with me. I will start -- approach this differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have a means of gathering information about what was going on in the enclave, people who would inform you of events, sources of information?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to gather that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In either May or June of 1992, did you receive any information regarding an attack on your hotel?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was the information that you received?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that Mr. Oric was going to attack me that evening, that he was going to ask me to surrender. And I didn't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you make any plans to prepare for that?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What plans did you make?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I held a meeting with my men. I briefed them. I told them about the situation. Two of my men said that they didn't want to participate. I told them to go, and I told them also that if we survived that they could join us again on the following day. Then I made a plan to take some of our men who were at home -- to send them home, actually, and the rest of us stayed at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you position men in a certain way around the hotel to prepare for this -- whatever it was that was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did Mr. Oric, indeed, turn up?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime early in the evening and the situation was really difficult. Mr. Oric appeared and he was issuing orders to his men. He was deploying his men around the hotel in shooting positions, and he invited me to surrender and he also asked my men not to attack his men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But how were you -- did you speak to him? Or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Ziga liked Naser very much, but he also liked me. And he found the situation very difficult. He wanted to go and talk to Naser himself. He -- and then I told him: You could get killed. He said: Well, if that is meant to be, fine. He left his arms and he left. He went to talk to Naser and luckily enough nothing happened and an agreement was reached for me and Naser to meet on the following day, and to clear the matter. Because it was really not clear why all of this was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Naser accepted that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Could the witness tell us exactly the names, the name of Ziga I know he may have said it already before, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Kamenica? Not Ziga?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kamenica. But his nickname is Ziga, Z-i-g-a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wanted that to be made clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You touched upon an issue that I want to get whatever information I can, and that's this. You said "it was not really clear why all of this was going on." During the stand off or encounter, whatever you want to describe it as, did Mr. Oric ever say anything that indicated to you what he wanted, or was any message gotten to you to give you some clue, some insight into what he wanted, what he was after?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He came to the hotel. You prepared for it. It's obviously a tense situation. There are armed men and Mr. Oric has surrounded your hotel. You've prepared for it, and Ziga Kamenica is acting as a go between. In the midst of this did you ever ascertain any reason why Mr. Oric was doing this, what he wanted from you?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not that evening. We did it on the following day. Ziga asked him to come to Domavija on the following day, and he indeed did turn up in the morning and that is when we clarified the matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Did -- I won't go into that. Let's move on to the second day when Mr. Oric turns up. I think you said he turned up alone.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you and he talk?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I suppose the topic of conversation or one of them might have been the events of the previous evening?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did Mr. Oric explain to you what it was that had caused the encounter?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He explained. He said that he was misinformed, that he had some men who provided him with false information. We cleared the matter. The situation was not tense. The conversation was relaxed. And we dealt with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, can you tell the Trial Chamber what the false information was that had precipitated this encounter? What he thought the ...

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Something to the effect of me being, so to speak, engaged in some activities, for example the reconnaissance of Zalazje made people go there, because they thought I was going to attack them. That was the misinformation. People went there. Some men were killed. I didn't have a clue about that. We clarified that. And after that we didn't have any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did just -- can you clarify something for us, please. What precisely was he saying had been the matter that had concerned him to the point where he gathers men with guns and comes and surrounds you at the hotel? It must have -- of course, it must have been a burning issue for both of you to resolve and you must have been very keen to know exactly what it was that caused this problem. So can you -- can you just give us a little more precision about that.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He received information that I wanted to attack Zalazje, that I was on my way there without informing him. Some Muslims got killed there, and that is why he came. But I did not have anything to do with that. I didn't go there. I was not interested in doing that. We had a good and long discussion about that. And when he left me, he was convinced that I had not had anything whatsoever to do with that and I, on my part, was convinced that he was surrounded with men who misinformed him. He invited me to his house, to a meeting that was going to take place in his house later that afternoon, to confirm to me the good spirit of that meeting that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see in the transcript, on line 20, that I was convinced that he was surrounded with men who misinformed him. But when I was listening to the interpretation, what I heard was "surrounded with a man." I want to know whether he mentioned "men" in the plural or just one man who was misinforming Mr. Oric. More one person was misinforming Mr. Oric according to you? Or just one person? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you will allow me, I will answer. I can see that you're taking things out of the context here and you can take my words in any way you want. I didn't want this war. I did not need any territories. I wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please, just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. We are the judges here. Not you, here. Just answer my question. When you were answering the previous question that was put to you by Mr. Di Fazio, did you say men in the plural or man in the singular? As being persons who were misinforming Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is why I wanted to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just answer the question in the plural or singular that's all I want to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More than one man. Men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's it. Next question, Mr. Di Fazio, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You explained to us the reasons that Mr. -- the concerns that Mr. Oric had or touched upon that topic. Is this a fair summary of what you understood, having spoken to Mr. Oric? He was concerned about you embarking on your own military enterprises and, in particular, others?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, you also mentioned a visit to Mr. Tursonovic's -- I think you mentioned that there was a meeting later that day, that he invited you to a meeting later that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that meeting that we had, Naser and I, Naser said that I should come and see him at Potocari, where his house was. And that there would be a meeting that day in connection with the attack at -- on Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you go to that meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you get to the house of Mr. Oric, and there did you see Mr. Tursonovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I came to the house, in front of the house, basically, and Mr. Oric came out. And he said: How are you? How is it going? And then, behind him, out of Naser's house Zulfo Tursonovic came and he said: If what Hakija Meholjic is going to be present at this meeting, I won't. And may I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Naser found it difficult. He was uncomfortable and he didn't know what to do and then I said, Naser, if that's a problem, I will go and let him stay. And then I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what was your understanding of the main purpose of your attending at Mr. Oric's house that afternoon? If Mr. Tursonovic had not been there and this little episode had not occurred, what did you understand you were going there to do?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you, when Mr. Oric invited me to come to his house, he said there would be a meeting in connection with the attack on Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I will return to this issue in Zalazje later in another context. In 1992, did you ever have cause to describe you and your men as being part of HVO forces? Did you ever have reason to do that for some period of time?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Just for clarification. Could the witness explain what the acronym HVO stood for, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Certainly. You heard His Honour's question. What does it stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Croat Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I want you to provide a short summary of how it came -- came about that you decided to adopt this strategy.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a number of occasions, I tried to act in line with everybody else and to fit in, but we kept running into difficulties. And we had a meeting at the town hall and there was a discussion about my situation, the newly created situation with regard to everything, and Hamdija Fejzic was the main speaker. And he said that when I was there everybody kept silent and when I wasn't there, people used to talk a lot. Then I offered them the army, but I told them to leave me alone. And then they said, "Well, your men won't come without you." I said, "You want my head? I won't give it to you." And then it was not going well and, therefore, I decided -- and let me point out that at that time, in 1992, the HVO together with the armed forces of the BiH were fighting Chetnik forces. So I said, "Okay, I'm not an enemy. I'm there as well. And we can perhaps discuss things on an equal footing. This is a war. A war is not a game, and you stand to lose your life." And I did not want to risk my life and I had to defend myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I think it is the case of having the witness specify exactly which period in time in 1992 this was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm going to get to the details of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because 1992 is a whole year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: First of all, try and put a time, a date if you can, if not a month, or at least a period of time in 1992. Tell us where the meeting was, where it was actually held and, finally, tell us if Mr. Oric was there, Mr. Tursonovic and any other members of the Srebrenica TO were there. So, time, location, people present. Let's hear about that.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time was at some point in the first half of July, at the town hall. Quite a few people were there: Akif, Zulfo, perhaps Naser. Perhaps one of them left for a few minutes. I can't remember. But at any rate, there was a meeting and there were about 20 of us there. And then there was this discussion. And to no avail. I offered my men, just so they could leave me alone and they didn't want to. And then I said, "Well you want my life, and that's what I can't accept."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did declaring yourself HVO actually manifest itself in any way? Did you put on HVO uniforms? Or do anything like that?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have any uniforms. We had -- we didn't even have a civilian clothes let alone HVO uniforms. I did not actually get in touch with them, but I was just trying to save my life. We did not have a direct contact with HVO. We didn't have a radio link or anything. That was a decision that I made in a given situation because there was nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did anyone at this meeting that you've described directly ask you to become subordinated to their command?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that period they kept asking me whether I would accept subordination or not and I said, yes, and then Naser invited me to come and see him and Zulfo wouldn't have it. So whatever I tried was to no avail, and once I've exhausted all of those possibilities I've tried everything and -- well, if you're interested, I even gave away food for the hospital, as I had been ordered and they still said I wasn't good enough. So I thought, what else do you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. My question is actually this: At the actual meeting itself, the meeting that you have been describing, did any individual tell you or invite you or order you, try and convince you that you should become subordinated to their command, at the actual meeting? This is when --

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You just mentioned providing food at the hospital. Who told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Naser. We had agreed that I would give some food for the hospital, the civilian police, and the civil defence as well, because people had been exposed to shelling and then I kept providing food until the point in time when we had no more food left and then of course I stopped as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber when you received -- sorry, when you did this, when you supplied food for these civilian police, civilian defence, hospital, these civilian organisations and bodies, when did you do that, approximately?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was from -- when the War Presidency had been set up, and they organised all those services. And then there was an agreement, according to which I would provide food, but everybody else would be bringing food along as well. So nothing actually happened along those lines. I provided food for as long as I could and it went on for two or three weeks, perhaps slightly longer for the hospital. But I stopped providing food to the police force earlier because I wasn't getting food from anyone. So how was I supposed to provide food to somebody else since he wasn't getting anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, Your Honour. It's a matter of the transcript and a question of interpretation. It may be a small point but we were just conferring about it. It's at page 27, line 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It says "and then Naser invited me to come and see him, and Zulfo wouldn't have it." Now obviously I think for native English speakers that colloquialism is reasonably clear, but I think the Bosnian was most effective, wouldn't permit it or would not allow it and it is a matter which, I think, does need clarification because "wouldn't have it" may be a bit ambiguous. So our understanding is that it means "would not permit it," "would not allow it." That's just for the record, and perhaps it can be clarified at some later stage; but it seemed appropriate to raise it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you for raising the matter. Perhaps the witness who must in the meantime have received interpretation of this exchange would volunteer to clarify himself. If you could kindly, because this is a question of whether the English translation and the Bosnian expression are in agreement, or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps not quite, but I can perhaps state it once again. I was invited by Naser. I got there. And Zulfo opposed it on the spot. I was present and he was opposed to my being there. Have I made myself clear now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, certainly. Thank you Mr. Meholjic. Are you satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, thank you. Yes you may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Further -- just back -- return to food at the -- providing food for the civilians, entities, the hospital, the police, and so on. Earlier in your statement, in your testimony just a few questions ago, you said you even tried to -- you're talking about how you were trying to please "them." And you said that you even provided food at the hospital, as you had been ordered. Who ordered you to do this?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, in our jargon, let's say, we have an expression for the order. An order is in writing, or else somebody tells you to do something. I did not get an order in writing, but I was told to provide food for the police force, the tribunal, the hospital, and the civil defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's okay. I understand that. But who actually told you to do that? Who was it?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naser told me. He said, "That's what you're going to do."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you did so?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just complement this. I don't know if it is of essential importance, but with the proviso that Zulfo and Naser and all the local commanders would also accept the idea that they would be bringing food along. So as to have a centre where all this food could be prepared. We had a kitchen and so we could organise it that way. But afterwards, nobody else brought any food and basically I myself didn't have anything to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just one more question about the encounter with Mr. Oric at his home in Potocari, when Zulfo Tursonovic was there and when the -- when you left, because of Mr. Tursonovic's attitude. On that occasion, were you ordered to leave by anyone? Or did you leave voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move to another topic. You've, earlier in your evidence this morning, you touched upon the issue of the institution of civil authorities and you've told us about what you proposed at that meeting; that was discussed. Can you tell us if, in 1992, you became aware of a War Presidency having been formed?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember about when you became aware it had been formed?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps on the same day and perhaps a couple of days later, but mostly it was known at Srebrenica what was going on. It was no secret. Srebrenica is a small town. And the peoples' mentalities, a little bit like they want to know everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sure. Let's just be clear. You say "perhaps the same day or perhaps a couple of days later." Are you talking about the same day as the meeting where you expressed your views about civilian authorities? Is that the day that you're talking about? You have to answer "yes" so it gets recorded into the transcript or -- sorry you have to answer "yes" or "no." You have to answer so it gets recorded.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the same day when the meeting was held and the meeting was held at a later stage. Not on that day. Perhaps mid July or later that the meeting was held, where the War Presidency was elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm a little bit confused so let's be real clear about this. There was a meeting that you've already told us about that you attended where you discussed the -- your -- you aired your views about the establishment, the need to establish civilian authorities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Subsequently, after that meeting, did you become aware that a War Presidency had been formed? Am I correct or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not at that meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- where I was. A couple of days later the elections took place. I don't know if you understand what I'm saying. Not on the same day when I attended the meeting at Domavija, but -- and then I left. It was not elected on that day, but a couple of days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And you just mentioned elections. Did you actually mean elections in the sense of people going along a ballot box and put -- put -- putting their votes in?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no elections as such. It would have been impossible to organise the elections. People from the staff sat down together. They invited some citizens, some honorable citizens or some members of the armed forces and they decided to agree and set up a War Presidency because presumably they had grasped the fact that they had to set up something like that. This is just an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that no elections actually took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, do I understand correctly that you played no part in the creation of or the appointment of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I attended or participated in no meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm going to go on to a document now that will probably occupy me probably occupy me for two or three minutes. Can we break now and deal with it discretely?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Di Fazio. We will have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's continue, Mr. Di Fazio, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We were talking about the War Presidency, starting to talk about the War Presidency, just before the break. I asked you about elections and you answered that there were no elections. It would have been impossible to organise the elections. And then you said: "People from the staff sat down together. They invited some citizens, some honourable citizens or some members of the armed forces and they decided to agree and set up a War Presidency." Now, people from the staff, what staff are you talking about there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness said that this was his assumption, that he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic is correct, because I do recall the witness saying that he assumed -- he assumed this. But perhaps you can re-draft your question and go back a little bit to the previous --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And see whether this was a reasoned assessment or whether it was just --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, okay. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- a fruit of just -- BY MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the course of your answer you definitely said that there was -- the staff invited people to form a War Presidency. First of all, is that something you know? Or is that an assumption, something you're guessing at?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nobody else there to invite people. Somebody had to do it. It could not have been a group of citizens, random citizens. Somebody had to organise all this. And I don't see anything in dispute here. Since there was no civilian authority, somebody had to organise this. It could not have just happened by chance and this is my assumption. And for that reason, I cannot claim that this was happening that way. I was not present there. I don't know how the elections went and how they were governed. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now we know basically that this was a reasoned assumption sort of, so you can regulate your next question accordingly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, now, we have -- we now know the basis for your conclusions and why you drew that. Now, apart from your reasoning that you just explained to us now, did you ever hear or see anything, possibly even subsequently, that confirmed your assumption that the War Presidency -- sorry, that the staff, the Srebrenica staff invited this people to this meeting to set up a War Presidency? So did anyone ever say anything to you that led you to the same conclusion?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in conversation with Djemo Becirovic who became a member of the War Presidency, I learned that they had been invited people who made up the Territorial Defence staff were invited to meet and to set up a War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And who was Djemo Becirovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djemo Becirovic was the head of the sector for economy. That was his position in the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can the witness be shown Exhibit P42. Your Honours have it in the Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just have a look at that document. Cast your eye over it. And then I will take you to various parts of it. Now my first question is, prior to coming to The Hague, had you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Read the first paragraph, the very first paragraph. Now, you've just moments ago explained your assumption and what you heard from Djemo Becirovic regarding the role of the Srebrenica TO and the formation of the War Presidency. The first paragraph says here that "pursuant to the decision of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, at the initiative of the armed forces and citizens of the free territory of Srebrenica, the following was adopted. Decision ..." And then it goes on to talk about the decision. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now you already mentioned to the Trial Chamber what you thought about the role of the Srebrenica TO but what about the citizens of the free territory of Srebrenica. Are you aware of the citizens of the free territory of Srebrenica ever playing any role in the creation or the decision to create the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. I suppose that these people invited some other people that they held in high esteem, because of what they had done before, because of the reputation that they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was impossible to organise that with any random citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sure, okay. Thank you. Now, can I take you to article 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me for one moment. I might be able to shorten this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just look at the numbers 1 down to 11, starting with Hajrudin Avdic, Hamdija Fejzic and ending with Senahid Tabakovic. Do you see all of those names there?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Number 9 I think reads "Sefik Mandzic", correct, with an "S"?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sefik Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the time that you were in Srebrenica in 1992 and in the years thereafter -- let me with withdraw that and let me rephrase my question. Are all of those people there, who are listed, numbers 1 through to 11, were they members of the War Presidency as far as you were aware, as far as you were aware?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you know them all personally?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Go to -- I now want to take you through articles 5 to 11. Those names occur in that list that I've just taken you to. So go to Article 5. You've already told us you know Hajrudin. As far as you were aware, was he president of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Resid Efendic. As far as you were aware, was he secretary of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a brief period of time, after which he joined the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Article 7 relates to Mr. Oric and it doesn't say that he's in the War Presidency. It just says he's "hereby appointed commander of the Armed Forces Staff." You've already testified about that. But, did you understand him to be a member of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Hamdija Fejzic. Was he, indeed, chairman of the executive committee?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Djemo Becirevic was he secretary of the Secretariat for the Economy and Social Services?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you can quickly get through the next two, Becir Bogilovic and Jusuf Halilovic, were they in fact Public Security Station and Civilian Protection Staff respectively?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Trial Chamber the basis for your saying that, for making -- for confirming what is written here on the documents? In other words, how do you know, how do you know, what's your source of information as to the positions these people occupied in the War Presidency? Now I know Srebrenica was a small town. But just briefly tell the Trial Chamber what sort of access to information that you had, anyone that you might have spoken to, that allows you to say, well, yes, for example Hajrudin Avdic was the president. What are your sources of information?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody in Srebrenica knew that. He came to work in the municipality. He introduced himself as the president of the Presidency. Everybody referred to him as that. Everybody in Srebrenica knew that Hajrudin Avdic was the president of the Presidency. It was no secret. Nothing was done behind the closed door. The municipality assumed its functions and these people started working in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry. Would Your Honours just bear with me for one moment. All right. Thank you. Let's go back to Articles 5 through to 11. Can you tell the Trial Chamber if Hajrudin Avdic was in the Srebrenica TO, or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He had to do something with the command in Zulfo's territory, where Zulfo's army was. He occupied a position there. He had something to do with the staff or something else. He was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. But your position is that he was not a member of the Srebrenica TO? Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of him being a member of the TO Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about Resid Efendic mentioned in article 6, was he a member of the Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry it's just as to the date of this document. It's unclear what dates we're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a very fair comment. I don't take it as an objection, I take it as a contribution, actually. Thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Good point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's good. Can you put a date on it, on Mr. Resid Efendic. Was he a member of the Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if so, when.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, and if so, when. Prior to July 1992.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm confused. I don't know that Resid was a member of any military formations or that he was a member of any staffs. We're talking about the Presidency here, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, we are. But I'm asking you this: Do you know if Resid Efendic was a member of the Srebrenica TO prior to or up to July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Naser Oric we know about. What about Hamdija Fejzic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right. What about Djemo Rudin -- Becirovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't a member. He was a commander in his village that belonged to Zulfo's territory. The name of that village is Slatina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was he a commander of?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of a group of people. Either it was a platoon or some other sort of formation. I don't know what they called it at the time, because there was no organisation as such in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So he was a commander of a group of fighting men, is that correct, or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That group of fighting men was under command of Zulfo Tursunovic, Tursunovic; correct or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He was the commander of that group of fighting men and under the command of Zulfo Tursunovic prior to July of 1992, correct or not?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the objection -- the witness said that he doesn't know what was going on in that area and the Prosecution is asking leading questions, leading the witness to say that there was a relationship of subordination to this man, Zulfo Tursunovic. Whereas the witness never said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But if you look at page 40, line 5, regarding this Becirevic, the witness says he wasn't a member, I assume of the staff, Srebrenica Staff. He was a commander in his village that belonged to Zulfo's territory. The name of that village is Slatina and what was he a commander of. Then he says "of a group of people. Either it was a platoon or some other sort of formation. I don't know what they called it at the time because there was no organisation as such in place." Where Mr. Di Fazio then oversteps his -- he suddenly characterises this group as being a group of fighting men, which is something the witness never said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But of course I let him say it because you did not object at the time, so ... But in reality you are right only there. As far as the other contention, I don't think you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I perhaps should have rephrased my -- should have phrased my question: Was he the commander of a group of fighting men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are free to ask the witness. He is your witness not mine. We interfere only when it's necessary. And over here it is even less tight than it is in our domestic jurisdictions. So, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Jusuf Halilovic, was he a member of the Srebrenica TO prior to July of -- and up to July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Go back to article 4. Was Mirsa Dudic a member of the Srebrenica TO prior to July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. If the list that you gave me is valid, then you will find his name on that list. At that moment I did not know all these men. This was all happening rather quickly. In any case, he was a commander up there in Osmace village. I don't know what his position and duties were. In any case, he was a member of the army and he was a member of the BiH army, such as it was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Prior to July of 1992 or in the period of time leading up to July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there even later. He was in the army throughout all this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Aziz Nekic, was he a member of the Srebrenica TO in the period of time prior to July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with P42. Actually, I'm sorry. I do apologise. I wonder if P42 could be left with the witness and we could also produce P270.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, prior to coming to The Hague, had you seen Exhibit P270, the document that's just been placed in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just have a look at the document. You've already mentioned most of the names and the positions that these -- that we can see on P270. One that I don't think you've mentioned is Sefik Mandzic. Do you see that in the second paragraph of Exhibit P270, towards the end of that paragraph, talking about members of the War Presidency? You see Mirsad Dudic, Senahid Tabakovic and Sefik Mandzic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was Sefik Mandzic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sefik Mandzic was a commander up there. Of the part called Kraglijivoda, or Osak Kraglijivoda. In any case, that is the area. I don't know how it is referred to in documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber if prior to July of 1992 he was a member of the Srebrenica TO forces?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Until the day when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And when was he killed?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed in the autumn of 1992, in Fakovici during the fighting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. The next paragraph you've -- there's a name you already mentioned, Mirzet Halilovic. You see, the document claims that a decision has been made to form wartime military police and Mirzet Halilovic is appointed commander. That's what the document says. Now thinking back, using your own memory of those events, and bearing in mind you've testified that Mirzet Halilovic was a commander of the military police, can you tell us if he was in charge of the military police around July of 1992, or early July of 1992, as this document apparently asserts?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just give me a moment to confer with my colleagues, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to ask you some -- for some general comments about meetings that you may have or may not have attended in 1992. Firstly, you've already mentioned in your evidence a number of encounters at meetings that you had with Mr. -- where Mr. Tursonovic and Mr. Oric were present. In addition to all of the meetings that you've mentioned so far, at the Domavija hotel, encounters at his house, did you from time to time attend other meetings or other assemblies of men, large or small, where both Mr. Oric and Mr. Tursonovic were present? I'm talking about 1992 and going into early 1993, up until March of 1993.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the War Presidency, I was never invited or participated in their meetings. I did, however, participate in the meetings that were organised by the TO Staff, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And during those occasions, were there times when you were present with men such as Akif Ustic, Zulfo Tursonovic, Naser Oric all being together in the same room, along with other men, from time to time, 1992 up to March 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
