utterances.text: During those meetings where all of these men are gathered, were there discussions involving military issues, military matters?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At such meetings where all of those men are gathered, were there also discussions about other matters not involving military issues? Matters touching upon issues within the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, and I don't know. It's a bit unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I would prefer you to ask a direct question, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can't in this particular circumstance, Mr. Meholjic, but just bear with me. Were you able to, on these occasions that you were at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. meetings with other men and those three mention that I've mentioned, Mr. Oric, Mr. Tursonovic, Mr. Ustic, were you able to observe and see how those three men interacted with the other men gathered in meetings, interacted with you and the other men.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. We talked as people normally talk, depending on the situation. Sometimes you raise your voice. Sometimes you don't. But it depends on the overall atmosphere, on the circumstances around you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. That's exactly what I wanted to know. Thank you very much. So can you comment on any ability on the part of Mr. Oric, or lack of ability, to influence matters, issues at such meetings?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Everybody did. And especially him. I mean, he was a commander. He's supposed to have more influence than others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he exert that influence that commanding influence at these meetings where he, Mr. Tursonovic, you, and other men were gathered?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Sometimes he did. Sometimes he must have deemed that it was not necessary for him to do so. When -- I wasn't sitting inside his head, so I can't tell you what he was thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand that. I'm not asking you to get inside his head. I'm just asking you to tell us what you saw and observed, but I will leave the topic. Thank you very much. I want you to turn now to another issue and that is the issue of military operations. You've already mentioned -- you've already mentioned, in your evidence today, a place called Zalazje. And that was one of the reasons that you went to Mr. Oric's house. In other words, to discuss something concerned with Zalazje on the occasion that Mr. Tursonovic was rude to you and you decided to turn back and go home. Do you know if, prior to that occasion, there had been launched any attacks on Zalazje by Muslim forces within the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, it was failure twice and we had quite a few losses and so we had -- we suffered losses both times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. You say "we suffered losses." Do I take it that, yes, indeed, Muslim forces had attacked Zalazje on two prior occasions?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who commanded the forces on those two prior occasions? If you are able to say who did so, tell the Trial Chamber the basis for your saying that.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was in command, but I do know that Akif and Hamdija and Naser's people participated, because we know it on the basis of the dead, because of course you knew who had been killed. But even though -- well you're not asking me this, but we had to attack. There was no other way. They had been shelling and we had to attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting for one moment there was no reason for it. And I will get to that, the reason for it in just a moment. But what I am interested in is the command of the attack, the first two. You didn't participate in those attacks, I take it?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- when I say "I myself," I did not participate a single time. But my men on those two occasions that I know of, did not participate. But on the third occasion, when Zalazje fell, I sent my people to join in, although we had not agreed on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm going to get to the third occasion in just a moment. It's one very small matter that I just want to know. If you can't help us, that's fine. But the first two, the first two occasions involving Zalazje, you weren't there, you've just told us. Your men didn't participate, you've just told us. And that's clear. But do you have any source of information as to who commanded those first two attacks on Zalazje?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Akif and Hamdija's men took part, I don't know whether some other units as well. Well, since the people from Potocari were participating, there must have been a coordination there. But who was in fact in command of the entire operation of the entire action, I do not know. And it would be illogical that there would have had to be a staff that somebody would have had to issue orders. These are my assumptions, but I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. Thanks for that. Now, let's get back to the third attack on -- sorry. Before we get to that. Can you tell the Trial Chamber why it was that Zalazje was a source of concern to the Muslim forces. What were the Serbs doing from -- involving Zalazje that precipitated these attacks?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a village where most of them were soldiers. It was the army. They were heavily armed, from our point of view. They had guns, mortars, anti-aircraft, machine-guns and they were on a hill basically and it is above Srebrenica and Potocari. Since Srebrenica and Potocari are pretty close. And so they're halfway between the two. And the distance, the overall distance is about five kilometres. And they were shelling the civilian population on a daily basis. And we had to remove them. There was no other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do -- can you tell the Trial Chamber if the Muslim forces had met with any success in the first two attacks?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Well, it wasn't successful since we didn't manage to take the position. We felt many of our people were killed and we never managed to get to them either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. That's the background to Zalazje. Now, tell us about the conversation that you had with Mr. Oric regarding Zalazje and this is, of course, following the meeting or the failed meeting at his house at Potocari. When Mr. Tursonovic was rude to you, you left. Did you see Mr. Oric that evening?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And tell us where you saw him, whether he arrived alone or with others and what the topic of conversation was.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naser came to see me in late afternoon, early evening he came to see me at Domavija. He apologized a bit for Zulfo's behaviour. He was uncomfortable with it. But basically he came to see that there would be an attack on Zalazje and he told me, you know what, my friend, I'm a bit afraid of Zalazje. Would you agree to send your people to Zalazje and Zulfo will not be here. He will go to Alizovic [phoen] which was a neighbouring village and I accepted for my people to join in, to join his people, a certain number of my men. And we both talked to Kamenica, who was called Ziga. Because he too agreed and he was supposed to lead those men, and to come from the direction of Potocari. And, well, we agreed. And there was supposed to be no problem, with the proviso that I wouldn't be coming along.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did in fact your men participate in the attack?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you speak to Mr. Oric after the attack?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was the attack successful in military terms, achieve its objective?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a success. We achieved our goal and Mr. Oric came to thank my guys who had been good. And he said, had it not been for the people from Potocari and my men, they would never have made it, and that was okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: During the attack, under whose command were Ziga and the men that you provided?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was entrusted with the task. I mean, Ziga was the commander of that group, but in the course of the fighting he might have been entrusted with the task by somebody who was appointed Ziga's superior by Naser. Ziga was not able to lead the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Did Mr. Oric ever say to you that he commanded the attack?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naser was up there. I know that. And there was no blame there from any side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Don't worry. I'm not talking about blame on anyone's part. I'm just asking about command. The command. Command of Ziga and the group of men who go off to battle in Zalazje, were they operating independently or were they under the command of anyone?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a third possibility they were coordinating since this witness has referred to that. It is just -- it's a general objection that the question shouldn't presume that one person had to be in command. The witness has spoken of different units coordinating and he should be given the option of responding that there was no overall command, just different units coordinating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he was suggesting to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He said that already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He was suggesting to the witness. Let the witness answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. Mr. Meholjic, please answer Mr. Di Fazio's question. If you want, we can repeat it, read it out to you. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio referred to the command. And he said: Command of Ziga and the group of men who go off to battle in Zalazje, were they operating independently or were they under the command of anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Since I sent them up there, they were not allowed to do as they pleased. They had to obey someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Who? Who? Who did they have to obey during the attack? You weren't there.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had to obey Ziga and Ziga had to obey someone who -- I mean on the basis of my conversation with Naser, I sent him with Naser and it was up to him to decide who was to do what. They were acting in cooperation, but somebody would have had to command, to be in command, because otherwise the action wouldn't have been successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, with respect, that makes perfect sense. Do you know who it was, who that someone who would have had to command, do you know who the someone actually was? I'm not talking about the localised actions. I'm talking about the entire operation.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since Naser was up there, Naser obviously. Who else?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a placed call Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know if Muslim forces from within the Srebrenica enclave launched a military operation in that area, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't an enclave at the time. I don't know how you called that, but, yes, we did attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sure, okay. Well what I meant was that Muslim-held territory around Srebrenica. And can you remember the time of the attack? You may not know the date, but can you remember the month? If not the month, can you remember the season?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was in autumn, because we needed food.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a place in Srebrenica called Dom Kulture, or culture club?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever go there in relation to any events concerning this military operation on Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that before the attack or operation, call it what you will, involving Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was there?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were quite a few of us. We were invited to be informed that the staff had made the decision to launch an attack on Fakovici. There were between 20 and 25 people there, who came to hear what their task would be. And the meeting was chaired by Osmanovic, the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please not cover his mouth and could we have the second mike on because we can't hear him properly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was Akif, Zulfo, Naser, I myself, Sefik, Mandzic, myself. There were quite a few people, quite a few people who had some kind of army and who were commanders either of companies or units. It was a situation when everybody had to join in and do something, because there was -- people were starving there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Osmanovic, is that Osman Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there a discussion amongst the assembled men on how to conduct the attack?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everyone gave their point of view, their view of the situation and we decided how many men we could each provide.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there a proposal for you and your men?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I accepted, I could provide about sixty people and that I would go to the area stretching between just below a place called Skelani, below a place called Dziljebac [phoen] and we had to cut that communication link to prevent Serb forces from coming from the area of Skelani since it was at the very border with Serbia, the border is marked by the river Drina. And I was entrusted with that task myself to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At the meeting when you're -- when your tasking is being raised, were you concerned about the issue of mines in the area?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I asked for that because the date had not been made public at that stage. I asked for four days, for my people to go and demine the area, because otherwise we would be at the risk of mines, because a couple of days earlier a fighter from Ahmo Tihic, not one of my fighters but one of Ahmo Tihic's fighters was killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you. You -- you -- you asked for the four days. Was there any reaction from anyone?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Oric said to me "you'll get that".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please not cover his mouth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Meholjic, I am being asked by the interpreters to ask you not to cover your mouth when you are speaking, because your voice is not reaching them, because you are covering your mouth. Okay. It's a simple thing. Thank you. Let's go, let's proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Oric gave you your four days. Can you recall anything else that Mr. Oric said at the meeting? Any other matter that he raised, view that he took?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of the meeting, we were informed that the attack would be launched in two days' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who informed you at the end of the meeting that the attack would be in two day's time as opposed to four?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Osman Osmanovic said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was Mr. Oric still around at the end of the meeting when you are informed of this?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think that Zulfo and himself had gone out for a while. I seem to be recalling that. I think they were out and this other guy relayed the conclusion, but basically it was him who said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was your reaction when you heard it was to be two days instead of four days?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I wouldn't go along.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And briefly explain to the Trial Chamber why. Why wouldn't you go along if the attack was in two day's time as opposed to four days?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I thought my people would get killed and I would myself get killed and nothing was worth an attack being launched on a haphazard date. I mean it is not a defence operation where you have to do what you have to do, but if you're attacking, you have to make sure that you have as few victims as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: But just very briefly, tell the Trial Chamber what difference is two days going to make as opposed to four days? Is that linked somehow to the issue of mines? Or some other matter? Just tell them why. What is it about two days' warning as opposed to four days' warning that makes you say, no, I'm not going to participate?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because if I think in terms of Srebrenica and my seat, my headquarters, it was a long way away. We had no vehicles. We had to walk. So we would have needed a whole day to get there. And the demining team needed about two days to do that job, and then one day to come back. So sooner than four days I wouldn't have been able to make it. We're talking about 35 kilometres, I think. 35 kilometres away, I think. And it was not enough for me in order to prepare and I didn't accept to go with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just to be finally clear about this, you made it clear you weren't going to participate at the meeting, that's when you made it clear?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: After the meeting and before the attack, did you see Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to the Domavija hotel, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what transpired between you and him?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He says "You're not going." I say, "No." Then he says, "Okay. When I come back we will deal with that." And I said "Very well then."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did you understand him to be saying?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Either we would be arguing, or we would shoot at each other. I didn't know what to expect. In any case, nothing came out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did the attack, indeed, take place?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the area that I was supposed to cover was covered by Sefik Mandzic who was killed when he stepped on a land mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do you know who commanded that attack?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If anyone. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If anyone. If anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if anyone, obviously.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naser and Zulfo went up there. I don't know who was in command. Somebody should have coordinated the whole thing, somebody who was entrusted with that task by the staff. Naser was there. I don't know who was in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And you earlier mentioned - when you started to talk about this attack - that you mentioned, in an aside, that people were starving in Srebrenica. Just moments ago in your evidence, not too long ago. What were you driving at when you talked about starvation - as you were talking - and hunger, as you were talking about the attack on Fakovici? What was the point that you were making?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every member of the army, whatever that army may have been at the time, had their family and we all had to eat. People were starving, literally. Srebrenica as a town did not have any food and Fakovici was on a level ground up to the Drina. There was wheat and you could take food from there in order to survive and a lot of people did that and they couldn't care less whether they would die, whether they would be killed in the process or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a correction or clarification in the transcript. The witness said that it was an army of the sort which was not organised at the time. And this has not entered the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Meholjic -- are you finished Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not. Your Honour, the witness also said that people were starving. Dying of hunger. They were starved to death and this is what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You've heard Madam Vidovic make these two statements. Would you agree that that is precisely what you had stated yourself in your answer to Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The army was not organised. There were no barracks. And why am I saying this? You asked me how many people we could give for the action. I had men and I could give some. The others didn't. They had to go from one man to another to ask them whether they could go. It was not an organised army. It was not a real army and I can claim that before the God and the whole world that this army was not organised. It was not a real army and the circumstances were just the way they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the other part you didn't answer with regard to whether the people were starving to death. Is that what you stated earlier on in your answer to Mr. Di Fazio's question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When this was mentioned -- I'm sorry, you have to excuse me for a moment. I suffered through a lot and we had to do things that we had to do. And I'm very sorry that it didn't take part in that attack. I suffered greatly for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can cut this -- I don't think there will be an objection to this, if I make the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was the attack on Fakovici primarily to get food for the starving population of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really don't want to interrupt my learned friend. The witness has just said that the children were starving, but this hasn't been recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Did --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not trying to diminish this in any way at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question is the transcript should reflect what the witness actually states or what is actually stated. So is it correct that in what you have just stated in reaction to my question earlier on, is that children were also starving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that. And I had to eat what horses normally eat, and let alone the children; I had to eat oats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and thank you Madam Vidovic. Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Would Your Honours just give me a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a place called Podravnje?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Are you aware of there ever having been an attack by Muslim forces on that place?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us if it occurred before or after Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sefik Mandzic is somebody I associate with Podravno. He did a good job there. When I say "a good job," I mean he destroyed a military nest of an anti-aircraft machine-gun that was firing at people. There was this nest where the -- with a PAM which is an anti-aircraft machine-gun. Everybody talked about that, those who participated in that action. My people talked about that as well, because they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could we show the witness a map so that he could indicate to us where Podravnje is, in respect to Srebrenica, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't know if my map is actually -- oh, it might. Can I show you this map here. It's a new one. Put your glasses on because it is not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is west of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have a look at this map.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this be zoomed in a little? I can't see too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You may ...

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map has to be moved upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is it on that map or is it off that map?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is Podravno, and it is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Podravno has to be the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you to mark in pink marker text that I have here and I'm just about to hand to the usher the place called Podravno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's cut it short. Your finger was actually almost pointing to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here. Here it is. [Indicates] P-o-d-r-a-v-n-o, Podravno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And put your initials next to it, please okay. Can we zoom out now so that we can see where it is in respect to Srebrenica -- so it is south-west at 40 minutes south of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender this map into evidence and I may refer to it later and ask for further markings, but I've got copies here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right. This will become P --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P518, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P518, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On the map it actually says Podravno. I spoke about a place called Podravanje. Is Podravanje and Podravno, is it in fact the same place? Or is it just different --

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, did you attend any planning meetings concerning this operation?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But my deputy was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Velid Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he report to you or tell you what had been discussed or planned at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That Podravanje should be attacked in order to connect to Luka Zepa because they were wounded there. Nobody could assist them there. There. There was an interruption between these two territories and in strategical terms this was justified. And from there Suceska was being constantly shelled. They were very well armed. They had tanks and we had to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know -- sorry. Let me rephrase that. Do you know if soldiers or fighters from the Srebrenica TO command -- I'm sorry. Let me withdraw that question. Can you tell us if Muslim fighters from the Srebrenica area were intended to participate in this military action?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. This is a large area, a five-kilometre area. You can't take that just like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Do you know of an area called Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber if any fighters, Muslim fighters from that area, Zepa, were meant to -- were intended to participate in this operation?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was to open a road for them and it wouldn't have been okay if we were fighting and they were just sitting and twiddling their thumbs. They had to participate as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know under whose command these fighters from Zepa were?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Avdo Palic for a time. They belonged to us down there. But I was not a person who could say anything about that, because I don't know. Avdo Palic was the commander and sometimes he would come to the meetings down there, to the staff. And this is the extent of my knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, whilst the witness is talking about this, the transcript is still lacking something. The witness mentioned that Zepa belonged to them for a time, and on the record it says "they belonged to us," and there is a huge difference there. Maybe the witness could clarify that for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Meholjic. Will you confirm what Madam Vidovic has just attributed to you having said a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ne were under the command of Avdo Palic, I believe that they were some sort of a battalion for a while. They did not belong to us. Naser and Zulfo went up there to negotiate. I don't know what they agreed. For a certain period of time they coordinated with us, as far as I know. And I don't know later on what happened. I don't know what was the situation like at that moment, but I know that they participated either in coordination or whichever way the staff told them to, to do that. In any case, they were there. They had to be there during the attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with that, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, Velid, your commander, went to the meeting and participated. Did you agree that your men should participate in the operation involving Podravno or Podravanje?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Not for a single moment did the witness mention an operation. On several occasions my learned friend has used the word "operation" for these developments. The witness has never mentioned the word himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Meholjic, would you describe the attack on Podravanje or Podravno as an operation, in military terms? Or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not a military expert. I have very little experience, negligible experience. And knowledge that dates before -- from before the war, when I served in the JNA. We called this an action. An action to liberate Podravanje. And this is the terminology that we used and you can call it whatever you want to call it. We never used the term "operation." An operation means something huge and we were not involved in anything huge. We were just little people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well maybe that's been source -- in fact, if I can allay Madam Vidovic's fears, I'm actually using the word operation in order to be as neutral as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought so as well. But now you have more or less a direction from the witness himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I will switch from operation to action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To action, yes. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In our language there is a huge difference and the witness may be confused if the terms are mixed up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In instances like this where there is obviously a difference in the significance or in the meaning of terminology from one language to another, it is important to have these laid out and clarified. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right. "Action" it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, the question, if you want me to repeat it for you, was -- I lost it now from my screen. It has -- I lost it. I have to go to a previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you contribute any forces, any of your men to this action in Podravanje?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Between 20 and 30. I can't remember exactly. According to the estimates we were given a task. We made a commitment. And we estimated that this is how many men would be needed to comply with that commitment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you or your men possess any Motorola radios?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Velid was given a Motorola of some sort. I don't know who from. I can tell that you're insisting on some details. This was a long time ago. A lot of things happened in the meantime. In any case, he was given Motorola from somewhere. I don't know whether this Motorola had been captured from somebody, not everybody who was involved in this action could have Motorolas. Only the people who were important could be provided with Motorolas. Velid was one of those. He was given a Motorola and from Avdo, the assistant commander from communications, he was given a coding machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want you to focus on the -- this action in Podravanje. During that particular action, was Velid given a Motorola to use?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who gave it to him?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody in the staff. He went there and picked it up. He was given a Motorola and he was entrusted with the task. We looked at the task, to see what he was supposed to do. Within that framework, as we were given this task for ourselves, we had to see what is it that we were supposed to do on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Excuse me. Did you ever understand, from Velid, what he was to do with the Motorola during this military action? Did he ever explain to you?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, when he arrived in the position from the direction of the mountain called Caurka, he was supposed to report to Naser, to tell him that he had arrived. I don't know what the agreement was about the beginning of the attack. There was some sort of tactics involved, as much as we could engage in any tactics, given our very modest experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us who commanded this action, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I want to be very clear, but in order to be clear I can't be short. And this is very important. If the Chamber will allow me. We were not real army. Somebody had to coordinate things as much as they could. And without that coordination, there wouldn't have been a successful action. I believe that Podravanje was a successful action. Naser was there. And if he had not appointed anybody else, then it was him. If he did not -- had not authorised anybody else to be in command -- Velid was not in command in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Velid was under the command of someone else at the action? That was your understanding?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do I understand your evidence to be that that person would have been either Mr. Oric or someone he assigned?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are two or three minutes left, because I saw you looking at the clock, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not finished with the attack but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you. If you want to -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could I break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine with us. If you want to go a few more minutes, we can go a few more minutes and then break after. But we are going to have a break now. 25 minutes from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. We were talking, before the break, about the action in Podravanje. Did you visit the site of the action after it had been completed?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you go alone or were you in company with anyone?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Nadret came with me. We went together to check it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just for the record that's Dr. Nadret Mujkanovic, I take it?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you go to a point in the landscape where you could -- where you had a good view of the site of what you understood to have been the area of action?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not on a hill actually. We were at Podravanje. Not really where the centre was, where the school was, but on the other side. And I saw a tank and I went to investigate. That entire area, I mean, the villages are not organised in the same way. They're a bit scattered as here, so you can't really say that there is a proper centre. The centre is usually where the school is and the houses are sometimes even one kilometre away and it is still a part of the same village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to point out to a mistake in the transcript. The witness said "I went to look what it was" and the transcript says "I went to investigate."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter believes it is the same meaning in English, but we do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right. I think we don't need an explanation from the witness so, Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. What I'm interested in is, did you have an opportunity, during your visit there, to have a look around and see either the entire area where the action had taken place, or parts of the area where the action had taken place?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in a situation in which I could see parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you see any evidence of burning of property? Any sort of property at all?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What could you see burnt?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw some hay, which had been burnt and dumped. And I said don't touch it. Well I don't know what the name for this is. It is some kind of a truck, because it's in -- it was in an area where there was a mine and that truck was used to carry the ore. And I said to the people "Don't set fire on it because it can be used. Don't set fire on it." Then there was some hay burning and I said, "Why are you setting fire to it? We'll need that hay." And they said, "Well Cica has told us to."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who is Cica?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfo Tursunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see soldiers there? By that I mean, people who you understood to be Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, we had no uniforms. People were dressed in rags. They didn't have either proper clothes or shoes, both soldiers and the civilians. Mostly the civilians were gathering food in the fields, pumpkins et cetera. It was in the autumn. And an army, any sort of official formation, well I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know what the ethnicity was of the people who were gathering food in the fields?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims of course. They wouldn't have been Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they people from the local area, or were they people who had come to the area?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, there were refugees from several municipalities in Srebrenica. From Bratunac only we had eleven-and-a-half thousand. Therefore, I did not know everyone. I was basically a foreigner in my own town and I just did not know everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I -- okay, thank you. During the -- your visit there, did you see a tank, an armoured vehicle?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Mandja and another gentleman named Mujo?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know Mandja and I know Mujo, but Mandja has a brother called Mujo. Now what Mujo you mean, I don't know; there are quite a few Mujos.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I will approach this topic a little differently. Did troops or fighters at the area do anything in respect of this tank that you'd seen?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I approached the tank and some guys from the Ljeskovik village wanted to set fire to it and I didn't allow it and I kept saying "Don't set fire to it." And I could see that there were nine grenades in the tank and, well, we needed those grenades. They would have come in useful. And I called a man whose name was Zuhdo, Hajdarevic. He knew how to drive a bulldozer because he used to work in the mine and so I said, Zuhdo, could you try and drive this tank, because we had nobody else. And he was trembling a little bit and I encouraged him. And then he got in and he set it in motion and then very slowly he went down a road from this hill and we took it to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it is what happened in Srebrenica that I am interested in. Where precisely did you take it to in Srebrenica? To the Domavija hotel? Or some other place?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the hotel. I mean he was driving and I was riding in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was he one of your men, the driver?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: But he wasn't a fighter. He used to work at a workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fair enough. What had been your intention with respect to this tank? Had you intended to seize it and keep it for yourself? I don't mean you personally, but for you and your men.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I think -- well, I saved it and I took it down to the workshop and there were two or three engineers there, machine engineers. And they could have repaired it and maybe give it to somebody else. I didn't want it to be a tank unit and I'm not good at it, but it was the first tank that got to Srebrenica and there wasn't a great deal of experience. We didn't know what a tank was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I needed to know. And did anyone -- let me rephrase the question. Were you able to hang on to the tank?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Afterwards Mandja, Mujo -- well, they're all called Mandja and there are three or four brothers. And they were all called Mandjas. So if you ask me which one -- because they did have different characters. Different nature. Different behaviour. And people used to say, well okay. Which one. And they asked -- they said it was their tank and that Naser's people took it and they asked for the tank and then we gave it away and then afterwards it was sent somewhere else and nine grenades were used and there was nothing left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's okay. What I want to know is this. The Mandja and Mujo -- of the many Mandja and Mujos who were about -- the Mandja and Mujo who came to take the tank, were they men under the command of Naser Oric? Or not? Or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they claimed to be. They were from Potocari and they were witness there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: They were what? Okay I didn't quite get the last part of your answer. They claimed to be. I assume that you mean claimed to be Naser Oric's men. They were from Potocari. And what was the last?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They were with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: With him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here it says they were witness there. But he said -- I mean, the interpretation that I heard was that they were "with him." I take it like that, I mean it's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said -- perhaps I can be a bit helpful here. They did not actually say they were Naser's people. I knew they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But they said, give us the tank. It's our tank, because we took it. And then I said, "Well, if you took it, why don't you take it then?" And then they said they were waiting. They didn't know anyone who could turn the engine on, et cetera. But basically they were Naser's people who came along and there was no incident there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know what Dr. Nedret Mujkanovic's purpose was in going to the site of this action? Was it just to have a look and see what happened? Or was there some other purpose?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: To have a look. He was a young man. He was interested. He had never seen it before. And then another tank was taken -- well not him. I don't know. They found another tank in a creek and then he came along riding in this second tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who, Dr. Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were two tanks. And he came with the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine, okay. Were both tanks taken back, and were both tanks later re-taken by Mujo and Mandja?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. That tank did not get to Domavija. And it went somewhere else. I don't know where they sent it. I don't know. But it never came to Domavija. I had nothing to do with it. So I have no idea. Later on, I heard that Zulfo's men took it, but that's just a rumour. That's what I heard. I can't state that. But the second tank did get to Srebrenica. I can claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And while we're on the topic of Dr. Mujkanovic, you've told us that he stayed for, I think quite some time with you, at the Domavija hotel. Did you become friends with him?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Fine. And did he, in the time that he was in Srebrenica, become acquainted with other members of the War Presidency and other members of the Srebrenica TO? Men such as Akif Ustic and Mr. Tursonovic?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came, I did not see him. He first met with them. And then he came to see me one day to talk to me. He was already familiar with some problems between us, and I told him: Doctor, take it easy. You will be able to assess it all on your own. I don't want to tell you anything. And he knew all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. And what I'm -- and in particular, he also knew and was acquainted with members of the Srebrenica TO? Men such as Akif Ustic, Naser Oric, Zulfo Tursunovic.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he knew. He perhaps didn't know everyone, but he knew quite a few of them. He treated quite a few of them. He knew many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he spend time at the Srebrenica TO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in the talks with Mr. Oric and all that, he helped in the shaping of some things. And I believe that for a while he was in charge of health or something like that, until Avdo came along. But he did attend some of their meetings, which I didn't, and he knew a lot more than I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I will deal with the issue of communications later, but did he speak to you from time to time about communications that were going on between Sarajevo and Srebrenica, or any communications that might have been going on between Sarajevo and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On a number of occasions. I don't know how many times exactly, but he did say that there were talks with Sarajevo, with Sefer Halilovic, I believe, and with Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And would he tell you this perhaps at nights when you were at the Domavija hotel?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't obligatory, but he carried out surgery on some people and then they said he oh, do you have something nice that you have prepared for the doctor, et cetera. And then we were just sitting around and talking and then somebody started talking. It wasn't information provided on a regular basis. It was just the casual conversation, informal conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Exactly. Exactly. Thank you. But that's what I wanted to ascertain. So I wanted to know the nature of it. This wasn't formal contacts with Dr. Mujkanovic. This was just things that you learned in the -- as -- over time as you became more acquainted with him, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did he [Realtime transcript read in error "you"] become friends with Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because the transcript says here "and did you become friends with Mr. Oric". Was your question "did you become friends with Mr. Oric or did he, Dr. Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Dr. Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I thought. That's what I thought you -- I heard you saying, but the transcript is "did you become friends with Mr. Oric". It's not whether you became friends with Mr. Oric. Whether Dr. Mujkanovic became friends with Mr. Oric. That's the question that you need to answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's about the doctor, yes, of course. We were all good friends with the doctor. He was held in high esteem by all. We all respected him. As far as I knew, he was a great deal of support to us. So Oric, of course, was on good terms with him as well. I don't know of any disagreements between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want you to turn your attention to another action. Do you know a place called Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think I might refer to the map if Your Honours please. I've forgot the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May P518 be produced to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not on this map. Maybe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have a look. I think you can see where the Drina is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are just pointing, you are pointing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here is Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So for the record, the witness points a spot on the map which is marked as "Bjelovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I will provide you with, again, with a pink marking pen. Could you just find for us Bjelovac. Another place I want you to find for us is a place called Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to a spot on the map indicate indicated as Voljevica and he marks, he highlights both this village and Bjelovac with pink highlighter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meholjic, could you please put your initials next to each of the places that you have marked. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, perhaps if you will just keep the exhibit there, I may come back to it while I am asking you questions about this topic, but you don't need to look at it just for the moment. Was there any meeting to discuss any military action at this place?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And I should have asked you prior to that. Can you remember approximately -- well, did, in fact, military action take place at Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember about what time of year that was or the date, if you have the date? Or even the month.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in winter, perhaps December, because I remember there was snow on the ground. Whether at the same time or whether we had snow two or three days later that's why I'm saying it, but it was before the New Year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now the meeting. Did you personally go to that meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did any of your deputies or men attend the meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Delic Velid, one of my member, my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he later inform you what had taken place at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber what he told you had happened at the meeting and what tasking your men had, if any?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was agreed that we would attack Bjelovac, perhaps some other place as well. But I wasn't present there. But I focussed on the part that was the task entrusted to us, that was agreed at that meeting; that is to say, for my men to deal with the road links, Bratunac, Voljevica, Zaluzje and Bjelovac and to set up an ambush there in case -- I think we're talking about a four-kilometre road from Bratunac. In order to make sure that Serb forces could not come and provide assistance to the ones in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the area that we wanted to take. I mean, that we had to take because Zalazje and Voljevica is and enormous area that had been inhabited by Bosniaks, but we had too many by Bosniaks, but we had too many people at Srebrenica and we had to take people from Bratunac back to the area of Bratunac and that's what happened later on and then we can talk about it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, were these details provided to you by Velid?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you agree to provide men to participate in this action at Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how many men?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20 or perhaps 25. In any case, they were my best men. And under the circumstances, they were well armed. They were good enough to carry out the action successfully and to prevent those people from passing through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a clarification here. When he was talking about the area, he also mentioned Zaluzje and Voljevica. Not Zalazje, and Voljevica. This is just to avoid confusion. We would like to have the record set straight. In line 17, can the witness confirm he was talking about Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Zaluzje is the place in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did Velid inform you of who had been present at the planning session?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. In any case, there was the staff or people in the staff who were in charge of that. I can't say who was present. I suppose there were people who were assigned tasks, the command, I suppose. Not everybody could be invited to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And your men did participate in the action?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's confirmed that already.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry for repeating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who commanded them during the action?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzad Mustafic was in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, was he one of your men?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not have given my men to anybody else but another of my men. One of mine would always be in charge of the rest of my men. They were all my men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who was -- who commanded Nedzad Mustafic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mustafic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- Mustafic, if anyone, during the action, during the action itself?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzad was given a task and he had to go to carry this task out and if there was anybody from the command ordering hinge differently, he would have to obey. And that's the instruction that I always gave to my men. If they received another order, they had to obey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You haven't answered the question actually, because your question was quite different. Who commanded Nedzad Mustafic, if anyone, during the action, during the action itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was so far from where the events were taking place, that -- the events were taking place in one place and he was in charge of an ambush in a different place. There was no communication between the two places. His task was to stop the Chetniks from Bratunac if they started moving from Bratunac. This was his part of the task during that operation, and that's what he was charged in Bjelovac and the general area of Bjelovac. I don't know if I make myself clear. Somebody, Naser or somebody assigned by Naser could have ordered him differently. He could have told him: "The action is called off, you have to withdraw," or "You have to go up there to help the men up there," because if we wanted to do something, this is how things had to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have ten minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a place called Kravica?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that place the subject of an action by Muslim forces in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was -- did you or your men participate in this?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Prior to the action taking place, did you know about it?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked informally, but, no, I did not know that this would take place on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, you may not have known the particular day. What I'm asking -- tell us if you know or not -- that there was going to be an action at that area, in that area? Not necessarily whether it was on a particular day or not.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what were the sources of your information?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The citizens knew everything. Sometimes even before the troops. That was part of our mentality. People were scurrying for food. They would follow the army to get hold of whatever was there to bring back home to their children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Think carefully about this question and answer it if you have knowledge. Do you know who commanded this particular attack?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that everybody, almost everybody went there except for my men. My men did not participate. I didn't either. Everybody else went. I don't know how the command was organised. I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you speak to anyone in the Srebrenica TO after the attack about the attack?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did talk and I saw people carrying corn from Zepa, civilians from Zepa and when I asked them where they were coming from, they said that they were in Kravica, that Kravica had fallen. Everybody was talking about that. There was nothing spectacular or special about that that people wouldn't know about. There was no reason for people not to know. Yes, I did talk to people and I also talked to Dr. Nadret and Djemo and Hamdija. And there was nothing to hide. There was nothing special going on that should have been hidden.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. I'm not suggesting there was. Did you ever discuss the attack with Zulfo Tursunovic or Akif Ustic or Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Akif Ustic was dead. I couldn't talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as for Zulfo, yes, I did talk to him later on. Sometimes we talked informally. And I was told that a lot more civilians entered than the troops even before the troops. They entered the village directly. They were supposed to stay outside the village. It was at the dawn of the 7th of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. In your conversations with Zulfo Tursonovic, did he say anything about participating, or not participating, in the actual attack? In other words, did he give you to understand that he'd been there and participated? Or did he say something that indicated he hadn't been? Or you can't say?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would sooner say that I don't know. His men were there. I'm telling you I don't know anybody who didn't go except for my men. And if I remember well, if I'm not mistaken, I was told that I should stay, since a lot of people went there and in case of an attack on Srebrenica, I could put up resistance. I believe that this is what I discussed with Naser, but it was a long time ago. It was only logical to -- to link up with the troops from Konjevic Polje. The troops from Konjevic Polje participated. They had to be coordinated. When I say forces, there may have been only five men. I'm using some military terms, although I'm not a military expert. I'm just mentioning the things that I remember. So when I say "forces from Konjevic Polje," there may have been only five men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever heard of a grouping of men or an entity of men called the Suceska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was Zulfo's brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did the -- sorry. Did the troops from Konjevic Polje have a special name, as Zulfo's men did?

utterances.speaker: HAKIJA MEHOLJIC:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the only name I am aware of is Konjevic. People from Konjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be an appropriate moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I thank you, Mr. Meholjic. We will continue tomorrow. Where do you stand more or less in relation to the projected time you needed to finish this witness? Are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm certainly going to occupy the half of tomorrow. No question about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Okay, I thank you Mr. Meholjic. I will give you a rest now. Tomorrow we will return here in this courtroom and we will resume at 9.00 in the morning. I thank you so much. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of April, 2005 at 9.00 a.m.
